thread:
sophia: uploaded the quantitative results from the Mistral-7B quant bakeoff (FP8 / AWQ / GPTQ / INT8). summary + a packaging proposal below.

sophia: tl;dr — AWQ/GPTQ keep best accuracy on our instruction/Eval-1000 set, FP8 gives slightly lower latency for seq<=512 on our runtime, INT8 is cheapest but shows ~1.8% average accuracy delta (EM) vs fp16 on long-context tasks. full numbers in the link.

diego: link?

sophia: https://internal.redwood/optimize/bakeoffs/1767771234 — main artifacts: raw logs, per-model eval CSVs, perf traces.

maya: can you annotate by hw? want A100 vs H100 numbers separated (we saw different FP8 speedups on H100).

sophia: done, per-hw sheets included. quick extract: A100: FP8 ~12% latency win over fp16 seq<=512; H100: FP8 ~5% win (kernel mismatch). AWQ/GPTQ accuracy delta <0.3% on avg, INT8 ~1.2-2.5% depending on prompt type.

sophia: proposal for a new "quant-matrix" profile packaging that Optimize can consume: single manifest that separates concerns (accuracy metadata, runtime knobs, compatibility tags). idea is to make rollout tooling pick the best profile by policy (latency/cost/accuracy).

sophia: example manifest (human-readable; CI stores this next to artifacts):

```json
{
  "profile_name": "quant-matrix-mistral7b-v1",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "algorithm": "awq",
  "accuracy": {
    "eval_set": "instr-eval-1000",
    "delta_vs_fp16_pct": "0.15",
    "metrics": ["EM:89.3","ROUGE-L:78.2"]
  },
  "runtime": {
    "preferred_hw": ["A100","H100"],
    "batch_size_recommendation": "8",
    "latency_p50_ms": "42",
    "latency_p95_ms": "120"
  },
  "compatibility": ["runtime:triton>=2.8","kvcache:true","onnx:false"],
  "cost": {
    "relative": "0.62",
    "units": "tokens/s equivalent"
  },
  "artifacts": {
    "quant_blob": "gs://redwood-bakeoffs/mistral7b/awq/v1/quant.bin",
    "calib_stats": "gs://.../calib.json"
  },
  "notes": "Use as canary for latency-first routes. fallback: fp16 if accuracy gate fails"
}
```

maya: I like separating accuracy & runtime. couple suggestions:
- include a small "sensitivity_map" key listing top-10 prompts where profile regresses more than X.
- include an explicit "rollback_sig": hash of blob to prevent silent swaps.

rachel: on versioning: suggest a simple semver-ish rule: increment MAJOR for algorithm changes (gptq->awq), MINOR for quant params or calibration changes, PATCH for metadata-only edits (docs/notes). also add a "compat_lineage" array: ["mistral7b-fp16:1.2.0"].

optimize-bot: recommended keys for Redwood Optimize ingestion: ["profile_name","version","algorithm","accuracy.delta","runtime.p95","compatibility.*","cost.relative","artifacts.quant_blob","sensitivity_map"]. will auto-indexing on upload if manifest matches schema.

diego: rollout plan? how to smoke test before routing traffic.

sophia: propose rollout:
- 0: run CI eval harness (dockerized) -> must pass accuracy gate: median delta <= 0.5% and no prompt in sensitivity_map > 2.0%
- 1: canary on internal dev stack (1% traffic) with online checks for latency regressions (>20% p95) and sampling ground-truth evals
- 2: progressive ramp (1 -> 5 -> 20 -> 100) with automatic rollback if sliding-window quality metric drops >0.7%

sophia: CI command to reproduce offline eval: `python infra/eval/bakeoff_run.py --model mistral-7b --profiles quant-matrix-mistral7b-v1 --hw A100 --out /tmp/bakeoff-1767771234`

maya: naming nit: prefer hyphenated `quant-matrix-mistral7b-v1` vs underscore. keep consistent across registry.

rachel: add `compat_tags` for runtime deps like `trt:8.2,cuda:11.8`; also include `privacy:non-PII` if any calibration used private traces.

optimize-bot: uploaded manifest validator: `optimize manifest validate /path/to/manifest.json` -> returns exit code 0/1 and prints schema mismatches.

diego: one more ask: add a small per-profile "cost_breakdown" that maps tokens->dollar estimate at current pricing bands so product can forecast spend.

sophia: good call — will add `cost_breakdown.estimate_usd_per_million_tokens` and a simple `tradeoff_reasoning` field explaining when to pick this profile (e.g., "latency-first, short-context, dev-tier").

maya: after we settle fields I'll open a tiny RFC in the repo (docs/quant-matrix-spec.md) and a tiny migration script to convert old qprof manifests.

rachel: :thumbsup: set the RFC PR target for EOW?

sophia: aiming for EOW for draft.

diego: sounds good. if folks agree I'll mark this profile as `canary-ready` and kick off the evaluate job.

sophia: thanks — I'll post the canary job id once started.

optimize-bot: reaction :white_check_mark:
